app/src/pages/moves/[name].astro:15-30 — the fetch-or-404 scaffold (try/api/isNotFound/Astro.response.status) is copy-pasted nearly verbatim in abilities/[name].astro:15-28, types/[name].astro:15-27 and pokemon/[name].astro:19-31

app/src/pages/moves/[name].astro:78-84, abilities/[name].astro:55-62, types/[name].astro:75-82 — the '<count> Pokémon' + card-grid pattern is hand-rolled per page, with no shared list component for the Items scenario to reuse

abstraction_design.rationale: The data-layer abstractions genuinely absorb the real variation (forms, version groups, 404s), but the page-level scaffold is duplicated four ways and the card grows flags rather than extension points, so a new Items section would reuse helpers but copy a page's boilerplate.

findings.issue: The client script fully re-implements the frontmatter's filter, pagination, URL serialization, humanize (:146 vs pokeapi.ts:70) and card markup (:188-223), so every home-page behaviour change is a two-place edit and the halves can drift.
findings.suggestion: Extract the pure logic (filter, paginate, urlFor, humanize, card model) into a shared TS module imported by both the frontmatter and the page script, or drive the list server-side from query params and let the script only push state and reload.

findings.issue: The sprite URL pattern /media/sprites/pokemon/<id>.png is derived here for the payload and again as the default in PokemonCard.astro:22, so the Deoxys-style sprite fix in the component never reaches home-page cards (client createCard uses entry.sprite at :194).
findings.suggestion: Add a single speciesSpriteUrl() helper in pokeapi.ts (returning the default variety's real front_default, falling back to the ID pattern) and use it in both sites plus the artwork fallback in pokemon/[name].astro:46-52.

findings.issue: The fetch-or-404 dance (try/api/isNotFound/status 404/fallback render) is duplicated across all four dynamic routes (abilities/[name].astro:15-28, types/[name].astro:15-27, pokemon/[name].astro:19-31), so new resource pages copy it a fifth time.
findings.suggestion: Add a fetchResourceOrNotFound(kind, name) helper in pokeapi.ts that returns the resource or null and sets Astro.response.status, letting each page shrink to data mapping plus markup.

findings.issue: The '<count> Pokémon' + <ul class=card-grid> pattern is hand-rolled in three pages (also abilities/[name].astro:55-62 and types/[name].astro:75-82), so list-level changes (sorting, badges, alternate forms) need three edits.
findings.suggestion: Introduce a PokemonCardList component that takes entries and renders count + grid, keeping one place to change list behaviour.

findings.issue: Byte-identical duplicate of 404.astro; in server output Astro already renders src/pages/404.astro for unmatched routes, so the catch-all adds a second file to keep in sync.
findings.suggestion: Delete [...path].astro and rely on the built-in 404 fallback.

findings.issue: export const prerender = false is repeated in all nine pages although astro.config.mjs:2 sets output: 'server', where on-demand rendering is already the default (current Astro semantics).
findings.suggestion: Remove the redundant exports, or keep only those that document an intentional choice; the noise hides genuinely meaningful prerender decisions.

findings.issue: Two independent caching layers coexist: the promise cache Map (:17, used by api()) and the module-level memoized promises for the species/type/generation indexes (:99-107); changing caching policy (TTL, invalidation on data change) requires reasoning about both.
findings.suggestion: Route the index builders through the same cache abstraction (e.g. a cached() wrapper with a shared TTL) so policy lives in one place.

findings.issue: strict:false and pervasive any types (e.g. pokeapi.ts:94-100, 163-176) mean API shape changes surface at runtime, making refactors and extensions (an Items section) riskier than they should be.
findings.suggestion: Enable strict and type the API response surfaces at least loosely (Pokemon, Move, Species interfaces) so the pokeapi.ts seams are checked.

summary: A tidy, conventionally-structured Astro 7 app whose data layer and small components give it good seams: all HTTP flows through one module, features sit in single route files, and domain helpers are genuinely shared. The main editability tax is the home page, which implements filtering, pagination, URL building, humanization and card markup twice (SSR frontmatter and an inline client script), and the sprite/card derivation duplicated between PokemonCard and index. Page-level scaffold (fetch-or-404, count+grid lists) is copy-pasted across the four dynamic routes, so adding a parallel section means copying boilerplate rather than reusing it.
